title: Call Me Xumi
style: Maranhão reggae blended with adult contemporary pop; organic, polished studio mix with spacious vocals and gentle dynamics; relaxed one-drop sway, warm rounded bass, crisp rim-click and shaker, clipped offbeat guitar, subtle hand percussion and occasional piano fills; mature female lead with a clear British accent, understated conversational phrasing, layered harmonies on the hook, narrative verses building to an expanded final chorus.
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Born in São Luís, eighty-nine,
Island salt in the morning air.
Richard came from Birmingham,
A short contract, then he stayed there.
He taught his Portuguese with a Midlands turn,
And taxi drivers laughed with love.
Fátima brought her Mineira heart,
Pagode in her hands, and more than enough.

[Pre-Chorus]
Two worlds talking over supper,
Football, books, and plans to roam.
A name too long for schoolyard tongues,
But every road still led me home.

[Chorus]
Call me Xumi, call me home,
I learned to carry more than one.
Red and black, my heart knows where,
Sport Recife, always there.
From Maranhão to Birmingham,
I keep both countries in my hands.
Call me Xumi, I belong
Where all my different roots grow strong.

[Verse 2]
At five, my father joined two names,
A television craze, a joke that stayed.
Mum called it silly every day,
And somehow made the nickname take.
Blue City patience from my dad,
My mother’s lion, fierce and true.
I learned the table, learned the teams,
And found there was room for every blue and red I knew.

[Pre-Chorus]
Spanish came like open windows,
English summers, Portuguese at home.
Futsal feet and restless questions,
I was never built for standing still alone.

[Chorus]
Call me Xumi, call me home,
I learned to carry more than one.
Red and black, my heart knows where,
Sport Recife, always there.
From Maranhão to Birmingham,
I keep both countries in my hands.
Call me Xumi, I belong
Where all my different roots grow strong.

[Bridge]
Seventeen, the papers spread,
London School of Economics ahead.
Mum cried two hours, Dad said, “Of course.”
Then cried alone, beyond my view.
I saw the shine he tried to hide,
And kept that little truth inside.

[Final Chorus]
Call me Xumi, call me home,
I learned to carry more than one.
Red and black, my heart knows where,
Sport Recife, always there.
From São Luís to Birmingham,
I keep both countries in my hands.
Call me Xumi, I belong
Where all my different roots grow strong.

[Outro]
Call me Xumi, call me home,
Everywhere I go, I bring them along.
